_: Every number and name the game can be tuned with. docs/crawlers.xlsx is the AUTHORITY; this file is the default a fresh checkout builds from. build.py reconciles the two and refuses to build if a key exists in only one of them.

render.tile_w.note: Screen width of one square metre of ground. Twice tile_h makes the classic two-to-one isometric view.

render.rise.note: LOCKED SCALE: how many pixels tall one metre is. Everything in the game is drawn against this, so a 1.6 m crawler is 52 px tall. Changing it rescales the entire world.

render.occluder_fade.note: How solid a block stays when it is standing between you and the tile you are inspecting. 1 = never fades, 0 = disappears entirely.

render.side_shade_left.note: Brightness of the left-facing wall of a block. Below 1 makes it darker than the top.

render.side_shade_right.note: Brightness of the right-facing wall of a block.

render.height_tint.note: How much lighter a surface gets per metre of elevation. Gives depth without lighting.

camera.key_pan_speed.note: How fast the arrow keys slide the view.

world.chunk_tiles.note: Width and depth of the piece of labyrinth generated. 56 tiles = 56 metres across.

world.max_elevation.note: How many different floor levels the rooms and halls are spread across.

roll.attribute_weight.note: How much a natural attribute is worth in a roll. At 1, an attribute of 4 is worth 4 -- the number on the sheet is the number in the roll.

roll.skill_weight.note: How much practice is worth in a roll. At 1, a skill of 3 is worth 3.

skill.cap.note: The most practice any one skill can hold. Six, the same scale as an attribute.

learn.gain_on_failure.note: Practice gained from a FAILED attempt. Rule 1: failing is how a crawler learns. Ten failures is a tenth of the way to mastery.

learn.gain_on_success.note: Practice gained from a successful attempt. Zero: succeeding teaches nothing at all, so a crawler who has mastered something stops improving until the labyrinth gives them something harder.

learn.near_miss_bonus.note: Extra practice for only just failing. Getting close teaches most of all.

learn.near_miss_margin.note: How close a failure has to be to count as only just missing. Two, on a scale where a whole roll is about a dozen.

actor.count.note: How many crawlers turn up in the labyrinth.

actor.attribute_min.note: Lowest a natural attribute can be. One to six, like a die: 3 and 4 are ordinary, 1 and 6 are remarkable.

actor.attribute_max.note: Highest a natural attribute can be.

actor.step_ticks.note: How long a crawler pauses between attempts to move. 60 ticks is a second.

actor.height_m.note: How tall a grown crawler is. At the locked scale of 32 pixels per metre this makes them 52 pixels tall.

render.zoom_start.note: How many real screen pixels one game pixel takes up when the game opens. Zooming does NOT make the world bigger -- it makes the pixels bigger, so the picture stays perfectly sharp.

render.zoom_min.note: Furthest out. One game pixel to one screen pixel, showing the most ground.

render.zoom_max.note: Closest in. Whole numbers only, which is what keeps every edge hard.

render.max_buffer_w.note: Widest the game picture is ever drawn, before it is blown up. Caps the work on a very large screen.

render.max_buffer_h.note: Tallest the game picture is ever drawn, before it is blown up.

world.rooms.note: How many rooms to carve out of the rock. Halls are then dug between them.

world.room_min.note: Smallest a room can be, along one side.

world.room_max.note: Largest a room can be, along one side.

world.hall_width.note: How wide the halls between rooms are.

world.rock_height.note: How far the solid rock rises above the floor beside it. This is what makes a wall a wall. Tall rock hides more of what is behind it, so this and the cutaway settings work against each other.

camp.bedrolls.note: How many bedrolls the crawlers lay out around the fire.

camp.stores.note: How many stores the crawlers put up.

camp.windbreaks.note: How many windbreaks the crawlers put up.

camp.site_spread.note: How far from the fire the rest of the camp is laid out.

camp.progress_per_success.note: How much of a structure one successful effort raises. 100 finishes it.

camp.work_ticks.note: How long a crawler takes between efforts. 60 ticks is a second.

render.cutaway_fade.note: How solid a wall of rock stays when it is standing between you and a floor behind it. This is the see-through fourth wall. 1 = never fades and rooms hide behind their own near walls; 0 = those walls vanish entirely.

render.cutaway_depth.note: How close a wall has to be to the floor it is hiding before it turns translucent. Small numbers fade only the near wall of a room, which is what you want; large numbers fade half the labyrinth into a haze.

render.tile_h_low.note: How tall a square metre of ground looks at the normal angle. Half of tile_w is the classic two-to-one isometric view.

render.tile_h_high.note: How tall a square metre of ground looks from the raised angle. Bigger means you are looking down more steeply and can see further into rooms. Walls stay the same height either way, so the locked 32 pixels to the metre holds at both angles.

camera.swing_ms.note: How long the view takes to swing a quarter turn. This runs on real time, not game time, so the swing is smooth whether or not the world is running.

camera.tilt_ms.note: How long the view takes to rise to the higher angle and back.

anim.walk_ticks.note: How long one full stride takes. 60 ticks is a second, so smaller is a faster walk.

anim.walk_leg_swing.note: How far the legs swing forward and back while walking.

anim.walk_knee_bend.note: How much the trailing knee folds as the leg comes through.

anim.walk_arm_swing.note: How far the arms swing, opposite to the legs.

anim.walk_bob.note: How far a crawler rises and falls with each step.

anim.work_ticks.note: How long one swing of a tool takes.

anim.work_arm_lift.note: How far the arms come up for a swing of work.

anim.work_lean.note: How far a crawler leans into their work.

anim.idle_ticks.note: How long one slow breath takes while standing about.

anim.idle_sway.note: How much a crawler sways while standing about.

anim.turn_ticks.note: How long a crawler takes to turn to face a new direction.

render.light_ambient.note: How lit the darkest FACE of something is, once the lamp has reached it. This is the shape of a thing, not how dark the room is -- that is light.ambient.

render.light_diffuse.note: How much brighter a face gets for facing the light.

actor.gear_chance.note: How likely a crawler is to turn up already wearing any given piece of gear.

time.max_steps_per_frame.note: The most the world is allowed to advance in a single drawn frame. Stops a slow machine, or a tab left in the background, from lurching forward all at once.

render.outline_width.note: How thick the highlight ring around a selected thing is drawn. It is drawn UNDER the thing and half of it is covered, so 2 here shows as a 1 pixel line around the silhouette.

texture.floor_px.note: How big one square of the ground's grain is. The grain repeats every this many pixels across the floor.

texture.fine_px.note: How big the grain is on crawlers and on anything built. Smaller than the floor's, because a face is only about eight pixels across.

texture.strength.note: How strongly the grain darkens and lightens what is underneath. 0 turns texture off entirely.

texture.speck.note: How much of the grain is hard specks of grit and rust rather than soft mottling.

texture.seed.note: Which grain gets generated. Change it for a different pattern of grit.

render.min_face_px.note: Faces smaller than this many pixels are not drawn. At 32 pixels to the metre a crawler has a lot of surfaces that never cover a whole pixel, and skipping them costs nothing to look at and saves a great deal of work.

roll.dice.note: How many dice are thrown for an attempt. Two gives a bell: middling results are common, extremes are rare.

roll.die_faces.note: How many faces each die has.

light.ambient.note: How much you can see where nothing is lighting the way. Very low: the labyrinth is dark, and light is something you carry into it.

light.warmth.note: How much a lit thing goes orange rather than just brighter. 0 is cold light, 1 is firelight.

light.steps.note: How many levels of brightness there are between dark and fully lit. Few levels look painted; many look smooth and cost more to draw.

light.falloff.note: How sharply light dies with distance. Above 1 keeps the bright part close to the source.

world.metres_per_tile.note: READ ONLY. One tile is one square metre. Non-negotiable rule 7.

render.iso_ratio.note: READ ONLY. tile_w divided by tile_h. Changing this is changing the camera, not balancing the game.

figure.nominal_height_m.note: READ ONLY. The height the skeleton and the figure parts are measured against. A crawler of a different height is scaled by the ratio.

ui.hint_desktop.text: drag to pan  ·  scroll to zoom  ·  Q/E turn, R raises  ·  space pauses, , and . change speed

ui.hint_touch.text: drag to pan  ·  pinch to zoom  ·  the buttons turn, raise, pause and change speed

character.name_pool.text: Bran, Ysolde, Corwin, Maerl, Thessa, Odric, Vela, Garn, Ketta, Rhodry, Isme, Dunmar, Sable, Wren, Halgar, Nix, Orla, Tam, Brennis, Sorrel

floor.name: floor
floor.note: A surface something can stand on.

solid.name: solid
solid.note: Fills its metre. Nothing walks through it.

ramp.name: ramp
ramp.note: Climbs exactly one metre between levels.

stone.name: stone
stone.note: Made of worked or natural rock.

water.name: water
water.note: Standing water. Shallow enough to wade.

damp.name: damp
damp.note: Wet underfoot. Things rot and grow here.

unstable.name: unstable
unstable.note: Loose. Shifts when weight is put on it.

grim.name: grim
grim.note: A reminder of what happened here.

person.name: person
person.note: A thinking creature with the six attributes and skills of its own.

crawler.name: crawler
crawler.note: One of yours: came into the labyrinth, may yet leave it.

structure.name: structure
structure.note: Something raised by hand that was not there before.

fire.name: fire
fire.note: Gives light and warmth, and will go out if nobody feeds it.

shelter.name: shelter
shelter.note: Keeps the weather and the dark off.

store.name: store
store.note: Holds things so they are not carried.

wood.name: wood
wood.note: Made of timber: burns, rots, can be repaired.

cloth.name: cloth
cloth.note: Made of fabric: light, tears, soaks.

unbuilt.name: unbuilt
unbuilt.note: Planned and marked out, but not finished.

warm.name: warm
warm.note: Holds off the cold. Crawlers will come to it.

leather.name: leather
leather.note: Cured hide. Tough, and it creaks.

tool.name: tool
tool.note: Made for work, not for fighting.

charm.name: charm
charm.note: Carried for luck, or for something worse.

stone_floor.name: Stone Floor
stone_floor.note: Worked flagstone. The default footing of the labyrinth.

moss_stone.name: Mossy Stone
moss_stone.note: Stone gone green where the water sits.

shallow_water.name: Shallow Water
shallow_water.note: Ankle deep. Slows a walker, ruins what it soaks.

stone_block.name: Stone Block
stone_block.note: A full cubic metre of rock.

might.name: Might
might.note: Raw physical force. Lifting, hauling, forcing, and the heavy end of any tool.

agility.name: Agility
agility.note: Speed and fine control. Keeping your feet, quick hands, delicate work.

endurance.name: Endurance
endurance.note: Staying power. Long marches, cold nights, illness, a whole day of work.

presence.name: Presence
presence.note: Effect on other people. Singing, teaching, calming a panic, bargaining.

intellect.name: Intellect
intellect.note: What can be learned and worked out. Recipes, repairs, maps, lore.

willpower.name: Willpower
willpower.note: What can be made to happen anyway. Fear, pain, boredom, sticking at a hated task.

clambering.name: Clambering
clambering.note: Climbing, scrambling, and keeping your feet on ground that does not want you to. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

labouring.name: Labouring
labouring.note: Hauling, digging, clearing ground, and still doing it an hour later. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.) Bare hands cost 4.

wrangling.name: Wrangling
wrangling.note: Handling animals, and dragging people out of trouble whether they like it or not. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

building.name: Building
building.note: Raising structures that stay up. Knowing where the weight goes, and being able to put it there. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.) Needs a tool in hand: without one the job is 6 points harder, which on a scale of about a dozen is close to impossible.

fighting.name: Fighting
fighting.note: The one fifth of the game that is violence. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

ranging.name: Ranging
ranging.note: Covering ground: travelling far, moving quietly, getting back again. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

performing.name: Performing
performing.note: Singing, playing, dancing, and holding a room while you do it. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

crafting.name: Crafting
crafting.note: Making and mending: tools, clothes, meals, anything that takes hands and a recipe. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

tinkering.name: Tinkering
tinkering.note: Locks, traps, and anything fiddly that punishes a shaking hand. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

tending.name: Tending
tending.note: Nursing, feeding, and keeping people upright who would rather lie down. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

foraging.name: Foraging
foraging.note: Hunting, fishing, gathering, and knowing which of it is safe to eat. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

enduring.name: Enduring
enduring.note: Cold, hunger, pain, boredom and the dark. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

bargaining.name: Bargaining
bargaining.note: Trading, persuading, and working out what somebody actually wants. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

leading.name: Leading
leading.note: Rallying, calming a panic, and holding a group together when it wants to scatter. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

studying.name: Studying
studying.note: Lore, mapmaking, deciphering, and sitting with a problem until it gives. (Every skill is one pair of the six attributes; all fifteen pairs exist.)

head.name: Head
head.note: Always drawn. Eight sides and a domed top: at 52 pixels tall the silhouette is most of what you read.

torso.name: Torso
torso.note: Always drawn. Wider at the shoulders, pinched at the waist, and swelling slightly in between -- that is what makes a figure read as a body.

pack_v.name: Pack
pack_v.note: Sits behind the chest, which is what the oy offset is for.

coil_v.name: Rope Coil
coil_v.note: Drawn larger than life so the coil reads at 32 pixels to the metre.

charm_v.name: Bone Charm
charm_v.note: Drawn larger than life: a true-scale knuckle bone would be under a pixel wide, and rule 4 says it has to be visible.

torch_flame.name: Torch Flame
torch_flame.note: The lit end. glow 1 means it is never darkened by the room, because it IS the light.

campfire.name: Campfire
campfire.note: The heart of a camp, and the only thing that lights a room. Everything else is laid out around it.

bedroll.name: Bedroll
bedroll.note: Somewhere to sleep. The easiest thing in a camp to put up.

store.name: Store
store.note: Keeps supplies off the wet floor.

windbreak.name: Windbreak
windbreak.note: The hardest thing in a starting camp, and the one that makes it feel like one.

root.name: Root
root.note: Between the feet, on the ground. Everything hangs off this, and it is what turns when a crawler changes direction.

hand_l.name: Left Hand
hand_l.note: Where the offhand item is held.

hand_r.name: Right Hand
hand_r.note: Where the mainhand item is held.

back.name: Back
back.note: Packs, capes, bedrolls, anything carried on the back.

gloves.name: Gloves
gloves.note: Elbow down: forearms and hands together.

mainhand.name: Mainhand
mainhand.note: The tool or weapon in the right hand.

offhand.name: Offhand
offhand.note: Shield, lantern, or a second tool, in the left hand.

feet.name: Feet
feet.note: Knees down: shins and feet together.

trinket1.name: Trinket 1
trinket1.note: A small carried thing. Hangs at the left hip.

trinket2.name: Trinket 2
trinket2.note: A small carried thing. Hangs at the right hip.

collar.name: Collar
collar.note: A worn strap, buckled at the throat.

pack.name: Pack
pack.note: Everything they own, on their back. Carries more and slows you down: the trade-off is the point.

spade.name: Spade
spade.note: For digging, clearing and, at a push, arguing. Counts as a tool, so it is what makes Building and Labouring possible at all.

toolbelt.name: Tool Belt
toolbelt.note: Loops and a buckle. Also counts as a tool.

boots.name: Boots
boots.note: Knee down. The first thing a crawler buys.

coil.name: Rope Coil
coil.note: Twenty metres, if you believe the seller.

torch.name: Torch
torch.note: Burns bright and burns out. The most light anybody carries.

candle.name: Candle
candle.note: Barely enough to read by, and it does not free a hand.

normal.note: Real time. One tick is a sixtieth of a second. The first row is always normal speed.

faster.note: Four times. About right for watching a camp go up.

fastest.note: Eight times. Add a row here for a faster one, or delete one you never use.
